news.Title: 〈陸股盤後〉製造業PMI重返擴張區間 三大指數漲跌互見
news.Content:
中國A股三大指數周三（30日）收盤漲跌互見，中國製造業活動自6月以來首次恢復擴張，隨著政策制定者推出新措施支持經濟發展，為第三季畫下了亮眼句點。

上證指數周三收報3,842.19點，漲0.31%。深證成指收報12,887.62點，跌0.11%。創業板指收報3,135.28點，跌0.23%。

中國國家統計局周三公布的數據顯示，9月官方製造業採購經理人指數（PMI）為 50.1，高於8月的 49.8，符合經濟學家預測。

涵蓋建築業與服務業的非製造業活動指數意外重返擴張區間，達到 50.2。指數高於 50 即代表產業活動擴張。

這些數據是在中國政府啟動兩年來最大規模刺激方案數小時後公布；在上季經濟成長速度降至 4.5% 至 5% 的年度目標區間以下後，此舉大幅提升中國實現全年成長目標的可能性。

儘管出口表現具韌性，且人工智慧（AI）帶動工業利潤成長，中國經濟仍持續承壓。消費成長已放緩至接近零的水準，企業信心依然低迷，投資亦持續萎縮。

即便如此，在美中兩國同意將貿易休戰期限延長兩個月、減少了短期貿易不確定性之後，中國的外部環境已適度轉好。

news.Title: AI交易大退潮！韓股Q3暴跌18.8%  但今年來累漲60%仍勝標普2.3%漲幅
news.Content:
今年第三季(9月30日止)，南韓股市遭遇劇烈反轉，綜合股指(Kospi)暴跌18.8%，成為同期全球表現最差的主要股市之一，這場拋售潮發生在AI交易突然逆轉之後，此前押注AI基礎設施需求的熱門標的三星電子和SK海力士等記憶體晶片股成重災區。儘管如此，Kospi今年來仍累計上漲60%，表現位居全球前列。相比之下，標普500指數同期僅上漲2.3%。

法國巴黎銀行財富管理公司亞洲首席投資長Prashant Bhayani表示，南韓市場已成為投資者判斷AI基設巨額資本支出前景的重要代理指標，7月的劇烈平倉是本輪調整的關鍵轉捩點。

避險基金Situational Awareness創辦人Leopold Aschenbrenner先前對南韓記憶體晶片股持有大規模槓桿部位，其部位崩盤與散戶大量買入槓桿單一股票ETF同時發生，進一步放大市場波動。

進入Q3季底，新的壓力來自債市。全球公債殖利率持續走高，威脅韓股自2025年初以來逾185%的累積漲幅。法國里昂證券韓國研究主管沈鐘民說：「我確實認為債市將拖累股市，這是全球性的現象。」

Bhayani則說，7月拋售後估值已更具吸引力，但大幅估值擴張空間有限，「我們可能看到合理回報，但會看到70%？不可能。」

目前，SK海力士和三星電子的遠期本益比已降至4至5倍區間，兩家公司合計約佔韓股市值的一半。

Robeco亞太股票主管Joshua Crabb表示，更高的債券殖利率構成「逆風」，但晶片股已使用低個位數本益比交易，直接影響有限。不過，標普全球市場情報8月報告警告，市場對「週期性供應過剩風險」的擔憂可能給未來獲利帶來壓力。

南韓利率環境也在變動，該國央行正升息以壓制過熱經濟中的通膨，此前房價和股市均明顯上漲。沈鐘民認為，利率上升可能進一步拖累回報。

儘管宏觀環境轉弱，AI支出仍是晶片股的核心支撐。沈鐘民看好南韓晶片商，稱美國大型雲端運算企業將繼續增加資本支出，「AI公司別無選擇。它們必須花錢，這是生死攸關的事。」HBM是輝達AI晶片的關鍵零組件，三星和SK海力士主導該市場，傳統DRAM和NAND價格大漲也為獲利提供額外支撐。

另一方面，公司治理風險引發市場警覺。《彭博資訊》報導指出，《大賣空》原型Michael Burry的門徒、Pomerium Capital創辦人Phil Clifton在週二(29日)的信中警告，投資韓國必須「特別程度的謹慎」。

他指出，韓股中看似充滿高成長、健康利潤率的企業，但股東與管理階層利益常錯置。由於遺產與贈與稅高達60%，控股家族有動機壓低股價、囤積現金、不付股息，使股票淪為「沒有票息的永久債券」，少數股東難以觸及超額價值。儘管南韓政府推動財閥治理改革，Clifton更看好日本市場，認為日本交易所的改革已相當成功，估價折價尚未完全消失。

AI退潮後，韓股正經歷估值與宏觀壓力的雙重考驗，而少數股東保護問題仍是長期隱憂。

news.Title: 富邦證推出美股盤前及盤後交易服務　10/1上線
news.Content:
（中央社記者曾仁凱台北2026年09月30日電）因應美股規劃延長交易時間，富邦證券今天宣布，10月1日起推出美股盤前及盤後交易服務，協助投資人掌握市場重要資訊發布時機，彈性規劃投資布局。

富邦證券表示，近年因AI、半導體及數位科技產業快速發展，帶動投資人對美股市場的關注及參與度提升。多數美國上市公司財報、法人說明會及重要經濟數據經常在一般交易時段之外公布，使投資人對即時掌握市場資訊及因應市場變化的需求日益提高。富邦證券此次推出美股盤前及盤後交易服務，希望進一步完善美股投資服務內容。

富邦證券表示，美股盤前及盤後交易服務分別於美國夏令時間（3月第2個星期日至11月第1個星期日）及冬令時間（11月第1個星期日至次年3月第2個星期日）適用不同交易時段。盤前交易時間為台灣時間下午4時至晚間9時30分（夏令時間）或下午5時至晚間10時30分（冬令時間）；盤後交易時間為台灣時間凌晨4時至早晨6時（夏令時間）或早晨5時至早晨7時（冬令時間）。

未來投資人除可於一般交易時段進行交易外，也可以利用延伸交易時段因應市場變化，靈活調整投資策略，提升交易便利性與即時性。

富邦證券提醒，盤前及盤後交易時段可能因市場參與者較少，出現流動性較低、買賣價差較大及價格波動較明顯等情況，委託單也可能無法立即或全數成交。依現行規範，美股盤前盤後時段僅接受當日限價委託，投資人應於交易前充分瞭解相關規則及風險，並審慎評估自身財務狀況與風險承受能力。

news.Title: 《台股盤後》收漲308點/48K未站穩；月K連二紅/季K連六紅
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-09-30 15:53:29 新聞中心 發佈

台股今(30)日由台積電、聯發科領軍開高，加上中國衝刺實體經濟、定向調降PSL利率一碼，除帶動台塑四寶續強，並激勵水泥、鋼鐵、玻陶、電線電纜股出現近期難得一見的齊揚走勢，輔以電子權值股日月光投控/台光電/奇鋐轉強、面板雙虎攻漲停的助攻，加權指數一度大漲近750點，可惜韓股及NASDAQ電子盤午盤後走弱下，川湖/廣達見翻黑、台積電尾盤亦遭摜壓，終場僅收在47940.13點，上漲308.17點或0.65%、重返5日線，成交量增至8756.72億元。月K二連紅、9月上漲1811.66點或3.93%；季K連六紅、Q3上漲1814.22點或3.93%。

WTI油價走跌下，美國10年公債殖利率上日仍走高，衍生市場疑慮，導致美國四大指數29日跌多漲少，僅費半指數逆勢收漲1.32%。亞洲股市方面，因AI、半導體相關股嗨漲，帶動日經225指數今日以紅盤開出後，大漲超過1,000點，終場上漲1.94%；韓國股市今日由紅翻黑，KOSPI終場下跌0.48%。

台股今日資金明顯回流，市場交投維持活絡，投資人信心見回升。電子族群漲跌互見，台積電早盤衝破2500元關卡、最高來到2510元，不過尾盤急殺，終場收在2480元，上漲0.2%，台達電上漲3%，南亞科、日月光投控、創意、奇鋐、鴻海、聯發科等收紅。另外，光電族群也獲資金點火，面板雙虎同步漲停，TPK-KY、聯合再生、彩晶、冠西電也都衝上漲停。

在29大類股表現方面，今日以玻璃陶瓷族群最為強勢，漲幅達3.94%；電器電纜上漲3.76%、塑膠類股也有3.64%漲幅，成為盤面三大亮點。在跌勢族群部分，僅居家生活、通信網路、電腦及周邊設備收黑，且跌幅均在1%內。

三大法人動向方面，今日三大法人總計買超386.57億元；其中，外資及陸資(不含外資自營商)買超296.35億元，投信買超77.81億元，自營商買超12.4億元。

news.Title: 〈券商拚美股投資〉富邦證擴大美股交易服務 10/1起盤前盤後都能下單
news.Content:
富邦證券今(30)日宣布，自10月1日起推出美股盤前和盤後交易服務，協助投資人掌握市場重要資訊發布時機，亦即投資人除可於一般交易時段進行交易外，也可利用延伸交易時段因應市場變化，靈活調整投資策略。

美股盤前及盤後交易服務分別於美國夏令時間(3月第二個星期日至11月第一個星期日)及冬令時間(11月第一個星期日至次年3月第二個星期日)適用不同交易時段。

其中，盤前交易時間為台灣時間16:00至21:30(夏令時間)或17:00至22:30(冬令時間)；盤後交易時間為台灣時間04:00至06:00(夏令時間)或05:00至07:00(冬令時間)。

富邦證說明，近年來，人工智慧(AI)、半導體和數位科技產業快速發展，帶動投資人對美股市場的關注及參與持續提升，而多數美國上市公司財報、法說會和重要經濟數據經常於一般交易時段對外公布，令投資人對即時掌握市場資訊及因應市場變化的需求日益提高，因此，此次推出美股盤前和盤後交易服務，進一步完善美股投資。

富邦證提醒，盤前及盤後交易時段可能因市場參與者較少，有流動性較低、買賣價差較大及價格波動較明顯等情況，委託單也可能無法立即或全數成交，而依現行規範，美股盤前盤後時段僅接受當日限價委託，投資人應於交易前充分瞭解相關規則及風險，並審慎評估自身財務狀況與風險承受能力。

news.Title: 百萬獎金入帳！華邦電被挖「超佛心歷史」網讚：準備跳槽過去
news.Content:
一名自稱華邦電員工的網友在Threads分享，第二季單季獎金最高達100萬元，預估工程師全年薪資可上看512萬元，貼文曝光後讓業界同仁羨煞不已，不少網友直呼「難怪學長都不離開」、「準備跳槽過去」

受惠於AI需求帶動的記憶體缺貨潮，多家台廠記憶體營收都呈現爆炸式成長，而記憶體大廠多以當季獲利回頭分紅，本季華邦電營業利益高達300億元，若以一成獲利回饋員工，約莫4000名員工分配綽綽有餘。

原PO在貼文表示，「哇靠，太扯，偉大的華邦電，這一季季獎金100萬啊，一年的年薪14個月加上4季季獎金，且不含加班部分，用底薪很粗略計算8萬元，8乘上14加上400共計512萬元年薪」，令他感嘆簡直是「躺著數錢」。貼文曝光後，不少網友直呼，「偉大的華邦電，這季獎金太扯了！」更有網友幽默表示「該跳槽去華邦電了」。

也有網友在Dcard討論，華邦電在景氣低谷時雖不發分紅，卻堅持不裁員，待景氣回溫便大方補償、重賞員工，展現「願意共體時艱的良心企業」形象，「工作那麼多年，第一次聽到有公司會上修獎金比例」、「是最公正的台灣公司，分紅甚至直接公開遊戲規則」

也有內行網友表示，「以前聽老前輩講過，邦邦在最慘的時候，大概就是叫大家多關一點燈，部門的每一分錢都要斤斤計較，但沒在把人拋下的」。更多留言稱在華邦電為「低調又佛心的公司」、「難怪在華邦電的學長都不離開」、「準備跳槽過去」。

（封面圖／東森新聞）

news.Title: 【Follow法人】外資掃貨群創友達逾16萬張 中華化結親台塑集團卻淪賣超王
news.Content:
（下午4點45分更新外資買賣超個股）

三大法人今（30）日合計買超386.57億元，其中外資回補台股296.36億元，大買面板雙虎群創（3481）和友達（2409）逾16萬張，反手砍挾帶合資題材的近70年老牌化工廠中華化（1727）8千餘張，淪為今日賣超王。

外資今日買超前三大：群創、友達、力積電

外資今日買超前十大標的中，電子股、傳產股各占4檔，ETF占2檔。群創（3481）獲買超99,099張登冠；友達（2409）以67,780張居次，面板雙虎合計獲加碼逾16萬張；力積電（6770）則獲買超58,591張，排名第三。

傳產股買盤也相當積極，中鋼（2002）和台泥（1101）獲買超54,063張、52,829張，分居第四、第五名；中石化（1314）獲買超41,405張，排名第六。台塑（1301）也被敲進29,049張，躋身前十名。

外資今日賣超前三大：中華化、玉山金、0050

賣超榜則以電子股占5檔最多，金融股占3檔，傳產股及ETF各占1檔。值得關注的是，台塑（1301）、台化（1326）及旗下台塑生醫、台塑化（6505）及中華化（1727）四家公司昨（29）日宣布合資成立「台塑中華先進化學」，雙方各出資30億元、各持股50%，切入半導體先進製程電子級硫酸市場，為傳統石化業布局AI供應鏈再添一步。

不過，挾帶合資題材的中華化（1727）今日股價不漲反跌8%，還遭外資重砍8,650張，居賣超榜首，與台塑獲加碼形成鮮明對比。其餘賣超第二至第四名依序為玉山金（2884）6,294張、元大台灣50（0050）5,338張及中信金（2891）5,214張。

電子股占賣超前十大的一半，正達（3149）遭賣超4,098張、光寶科（2301）4,039張、華新科（2492）3,929張，依序排名第五至第七；TPK-KY（3673）與和碩（4938）分別遭調節3,787張、3,738張，位居第九、第十。

外資回補台股296億元 分析師「中性看待」

根據證交所公布籌碼動向，三大法人今日合計買超386.57億元。其中，外資買超296.36億元，呈現由賣轉買。

投信買超77.81億元，累計連續2個交易日買超台股達83.61億元。

自營商合計買超12.4億元，同樣呈現由賣轉買，其中自行買賣買超13.81億元，避險操作賣超1.41億元。

資深證券分析師蔡明翰表示，隨著美股那斯達克指數創高、費城半導體指數轉強站回季線，國際資金重新流向科技股，也帶動外資對台股偏多布局。今日外資買超金額與大盤收漲逾300點的表現相符，買盤仍偏向強勢股，顯示布局態度積極；不過，台股已處歷史高檔，費半位階相對較低，台股若要持續領先創高，仍須等待美股跟進，不能將單日買超解讀為外資將一路追高。

內資方面，蔡明翰表示，投信與自營商的操作邏輯和外資相近，對後市趨勢偏多，但考量短線位階較高，拉回時較願意積極承接，上漲至高檔則可能適度調節，也因此今日並未大動作買超。

台股今日開高後盤中一度勁揚逾700點，不過尾盤獲利了結賣壓湧現，終場僅上漲308.17點、收在47,940.13點，成交金額達9,091.62億元。權值股以台達電（2308）、南亞（1303）表現較突出，台積電（2330）、聯發科（2454）與鴻海（2317）也收紅，支撐大盤維持漲勢。

news.Title: Bull of the Day: Astera Labs (ALAB)
news.Content:
Astera Labs Company Overview

Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) company Astera Labs ( ALAB ) develops semiconductor-based connectivity chips and software that link high-performance processors, memory, and networking equipment inside massive cloud and AI data centers. The company's specialized semiconductor chips and software act as the "nervous system" for AI data centers, ensuring ultra-fast and reliable communication between thousands of AI processors like GPUs and memory. Astera Labs is benefiting from soaring demand for high-speed connectivity as AI infrastructure shifts toward larger rack-scale systems.

Gavin Baker Explains His Astera Labs Bull Thesis

Gavin Baker is the Managing Partner and Chief Investment Officer of Atreides Management, a technology-focused investment firm. An early investor in companies like SpaceX ( SPCX ), Cloudflare ( NET ), and countless AI and AI infrastructure investments (including ALAB), Baker is widely considered one of the foremost AI experts on Wall Street. Baker believes AI is not a market bubble but a physical infrastructure "supercycle" that companies like Astera Labs benefit from.

Baker's core thesis revolves around 3 themes, including:

1. Irreplaceable: Connectivity chips are irreplaceable bottleneck assets.

2. Leveling the Playing Field: NVIDIA ( NVDA ) is the dominant player in the AI semiconductor industry. Although NVIDIA uses proprietary interconnects, hyperscalers like Meta Platforms ( META ) are now making their own in-house silicon. As the industry grows, hyperscalers developing custom silicon will rely on Astera Labs to scale their setups efficiently.

3. Mispricing: Baker noted that Astera Labs has been falsely bucketed as a copper-reliant connectivity play, with investors ignoring its optical capabilities, leading to an undervalued stock price.

Astera Labs: Rapid & Consistent Earnings Growth

Astera Labs has delivered investors the holy grail for a growth stock – consistent, triple-digit earnings and revenue growth. The company has grown annual earnings and sales at a triple-digit clip since 2024, and Zacks Consensus Estimates suggest Astera will achieve it again in 2026.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

In addition, Astera Labs has beaten Wall Street analyst expectations in every single quarter since its 2024 IPO.

Astera Labs Technical Analysis

ALAB shares are currently clearing multi-month resistance levels on heavy volume turnover – a sign of renewed demand.

Image Source: TradingView

Story Continues

Bottom Line

As artificial intelligence scales toward massive rack-based systems, Astera Labs continues to cement its role as an essential bottleneck asset. Triple-digit growth, consecutive earnings beats, and a juicy technical setup back the bull case.

news.Title: 【台股前三季風雲榜】森崴小金雞慘跌7成進榜...LINEPAY、最慘鴻家軍全腰斬 上市20大衰股一次看
news.Content:
台股今（30）日迎來第三季最後一個交易日，《Yahoo股市》統計截至今日為止，前三季以來跌幅前20大的上市公司中（註：經還原權息值），以通信網路業隴華（2424）跌得最重，前三季股價重挫逾7成，此外，森崴旗下的富威電力（6994）跌幅也同樣超過7成，而行動支付龍頭LINEPAY（7722）、最慘鴻家軍台揚（2314）、前生技股王康霈*（6919）也都有50%上下的跌幅，進榜最慘上市股。

台股上市公司前三季累計跌幅的前10名依序為隴華（2424）、富威電力（6994）、正峰（1538），前三均重挫超過70%，後續依序則為北極星藥業-KY（6550）、銘旺科（2429）、LINEPAY（7722）、台揚（2314）、吉茂（1587）、波力-KY（8467）與英利-KY（2239）。

第11到20名則分別是康霈*（6919）、展達（3447）、康控-KY（4943）、晉弘（6796）、泰福-KY（6541）、瑞儀（6176）、百和興業-KY（8404）、川飛（1516）、驊陞（6272）與東科-KY（5225），跌幅也至少有近4成。

首先，王士維指出「高價熱門股估值修正」的LINEPAY，剛上市時股價還能維持在高檔區間整理，但後續因為相關行動支付的手續費補貼方案率續推出、競爭加劇，讓股價進入漫長的估值修正期，市場競爭加劇之下引發長線機構資金與籌碼解套調節。

LINEPAY並非基本面潰敗，目前在台灣行動支付市佔率仍穩居龍頭地位， 股價跌幅已腰斬，目前進入築底階段；但上方套牢籌碼沉重，建議等待平台整理放量、外資買盤回補再做右側布局

其次他則指出，吉茂先前因市場吹捧「伺服器水冷散熱 CDU/冷卻零組件」跨界題材，帶動股價飆升；然而發現水冷實質營收與客戶驗證進度不如預期，題材熱度退燒、獲利跟不上股價，引發失望性多殺多的賣壓。後續觀察水冷實際出貨佔比是否顯著放大，營收是否開始貢獻與認證相關消息，股價目前由車用水箱本業支撐，一旦水冷認證通過，反而容易出現轉機題材的爆發力，可長期留意。

此外還有，蘋果鏈錯殺的轉機股瑞儀，股價修正主要面臨 iPad/MacBook 導入 OLED ，擠壓傳統背光模組市場的長線隱憂，市場法人提前提款下修估值，但瑞儀最具高殖利率護體的題材，所以股價超跌反而是防守型類股的留意機會，且公司積極佈局車載、醫療及光學次模組轉型，後續可觀察毛利率優化是否開始浮現。

最後則是堅決避開的北極星藥業-KY，北極星藥業的下跌代表無獲利生技股的本夢比退潮，相關解盲與轉型進度無法兌現為實質獲利，遭特定主力資金無情撤出，籌碼渙散若再加上成交量較低的話，股價絕對不可因低廉而心存僥倖攤平。

news.Title: Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights: Advanced Micro Devices, Micron, Nebius, Alphabet, Meta Platform and Apple
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – September 30, 2026 – Today, Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights Advanced Micro Devices AMD, Micron MU, Nebius NBIS, Alphabet GOOGL, Meta Platform META and Apple AAPL.

Why Muse Is Winning the Agentic AI Race

Agentic AI Has Arrived

Roughly four years ago, OpenAI kicked off the artificial intelligence revolution with the launch of the "ChatGPT" large language model (LLM). ChatGPT quickly became mainstream, gaining millions of users in the first few days after launch, and ultimately becoming one of the fastest-growing consumer applications in history. Since then, Wall Street investors have gone on a feeding frenzy as earnings and sales growth for AI-related companies has soared, with AI leaders such as Advanced Micro Devices , Micron and Nebius delivering triple-digit returns over the past year.

Generative AI applications like ChatGPT and Alphabet's "Gemini" have soared in popularity. These generative AI models can answer almost any question and quickly create content from user prompts. Like the search engine wars of the late 1990s, the AI winners have likely not been crowned yet. Until Google launched in 1997, Yahoo!, AltaVista, and Lycos owned the search engine arena.

However, Google gained an edge in the search engine wars by delivering a faster, cleaner, and more comprehensive search experience. Before Google, search engines were essentially cluttered online directories and digital phone books. Conversely, Google's unique ranking and hyperlink system made internet search a completely different, more optimal experience.

Currently, the AI revolution is shifting from the generative wave to the Agentic phase. Instead of merely answering prompts, Agentic AI autonomously plans and executes multi-step workflows to achieve broader goals. You can think of generative AI as having the smartest person in the world at your fingertips to answer questions.

While generative AI is undoubtedly revolutionary, Agentic AI takes the technology a step further. Generative AI is akin to having the smartest person in the world at your fingertips AND willing to complete tasks on your behalf, all at lightning-fast speed.

Muse: Meta's Google Moment?

Over the past few months, AI product launches have been dizzying as tech companies look to cash in on the hype surrounding Wall Street's hottest industry: artificial intelligence. In September alone, OpenAI expanded the "GPT-6" universe, Anthropic released "Claude Opus 5.5," xAI launched "Grok 4.7," and Google updated its family of applications. However, Meta Platform's "Muse" launch is arguably the most significant application release thus far in the AI revolution.

Story Continues

In fact, within just a handful of days, Muse jumped to #1 on the Apple App Store and Google Play. Meanwhile, according to Apptopia app analytics, Meta reached 1.1 million installs roughly 10 days after launch, surpassing ChatGPT's 2022 launch. For context, before the Muse launch, ChatGPT was the fastest-growing consumer application in history.

Who Will Win the Agentic AI Wars?

Currently, three main players dominate the Agentic AI realm: Meta Platforms, OpenAI, and Anthropic. Tuesday, OpenAI launched Dots, an always-on AI agent inside ChatGPT. Meanwhile, Anthropic has emerged as a powerhouse in the Agentic AI space. Monday, news dropped that Anthropic's revenue surged by 1,088% in 2025.

Each of these agents can connect to thousands of apps, remember ongoing context, run scheduled tasks, and bring back results for review. Although each of these companies has garnered investor attention, has scorching-hot growth, and similar capabilities, Meta Platforms is likely to gain an edge. Here are three reasons why Meta is positioned to dominate the Agentic AI industry:

1. Massive Distribution: In technology, distribution is paramount to success. Between WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, Threads, and Meta AI, Meta has a mind-boggling 3.60 billion active users. For context, Earth's current population is approximately 8.3 billion.

2. Invaluable Data: OpenAI and Anthropic must rely on general reasoning and software utility. Conversely, Meta leverages its understanding of user preferences from its family of apps to understand what users want before they act.

3. Cost Undercutting: Currently, Anthropic and OpenAI charge fees for their agents. However, because Meta has a thriving, highly profitable legacy business (unlike Anthropic and OpenAI), can offer Muse for free. By offering Muse for free, Meta will rapidly scale its user base. Essentially, Meta is taking a page out of the Robinhood (HOOD) "freebee" playbook. In time, Meta will generate a profit by taking a small fee on transactions and payments.

Bottom Line

news.Title: 《DJ Insight》Agility搶登美股，人形機器人邁向量產
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-09-30 14:15:29 林綺薇 發佈

特斯拉（TSLA.US）、Amazon（AMZN.US）與多家新創公司近年相繼投入人形機器人，但美國股市目前仍缺少以人形機器人為核心業務的純標的。這項空缺可能很快會由Agility Robotics補上。

Agility計畫於今年第四季與在那斯達克掛牌的特殊目的收購公司（SPAC）Churchill Capital Corp XI（CCXI.US）合併，交易完成後預計以「AGLT」為股票代號掛牌，成為美國首家股票上市的人形機器人公司，募資前股權估值約為25億美元。

然而，公司2025年營收僅178萬美元、淨損約1.38億美元；今年9月15日發布的新一代機器人Digit 5，截至5月雖已取得超過3億美元的多年期訂單，但仍須滿足特定合約里程碑條件，並預計於2027年上半年才開放早期客戶使用，年底前才全面供應。

累積6.5萬小時運行資料，企業簽下多年訂單

Agility成立於2015年，主力產品Digit鎖定製造、倉儲與物流環境，協助企業處理搬運料箱等重複性工作。Digit已進入多家企業的實際作業場域，包括汽車與工業零組件製造商Schaeffler（SHA0.DE）、第三方合約物流商GXO Logistics（GXO.US），以及日本汽車製造商豐田汽車（TM.US）旗下的加拿大工廠。

目前Digit已在9個客戶設施取得部署承諾，累積超過6.5萬小時運行紀錄。其中，在GXO位於美國喬治亞州的物流中心，Digit已搬運超過10萬個料箱，執行任務時的準確率約98%。

Digit 5強化人機協作，擴大工廠作業範圍

Agility也把商業部署累積的資料用於改善機器人的AI系統、開發新功能及增加可執行任務。

Digit 4目前主要執行料箱搬運，下一階段的Digit 5更把升級重點放在人機協作安全與作業範圍。傳統工業自動設備往往須以護欄或隔離區與人員分開，Digit 5則希望導入人員持續走動的既有倉庫與工廠，降低企業增加設備或重新配置動線的需求。

為此，Digit 5新增人體偵測、視覺與聲音提示，以及獨立安全控制器，可在偵測到人員過度靠近時主動避讓、停止或採取安全姿勢。Agility也與輝達（NVDA.US）合作導入Halos機器人安全平台，並參與美國與國際人形機器人安全標準制定。不過，相關安全標準仍在制定，Digit 5後續也須符合歐盟適用法規並加註CE標誌等，才能進入歐洲市場。

硬體升級也提高Digit 5的持續作業能力與工作範圍。新機可反覆搬運50磅物品，載重較Digit 4提高40%；電池續航90分鐘，充電時間縮短至9分鐘，運行與充電時間比也從2比1提高至10比1，使每日工作時間可超過20小時。此外，Digit 5也新增可更換的末端工具，未來可依任務切換不同配件，執行機台照料、組套、排序及品管等工作，讓企業以同一台機器人處理更多作業流程。

估值25億美元，上市資金支應量產與交付

Agility今年6月與Churchill Capital Corp XI簽署合併協議，對仍處虧損階段的Agility而言，這筆交易是支應Digit 5量產的關鍵。

截至2025年底，公司持有的現金、約當現金及受限現金合計約1.05億美元。申報文件更直接指出，現有資金不足以支應文件發布後至少12個月的營運需求，公司持續經營能力存在重大疑慮。

若交易順利完成，預計可為Agility帶來超過6.2億美元資金。其中約4.2億美元來自Churchill XI的信託帳戶，但須以SPAC股東未選擇贖回為前提；另有約2億美元私募股權投資（PIPE）由鴻海（2317）領投。

Agility計畫把這筆資金用於履行既有訂單、擴大客戶部署及提高Digit 5產量，接下來能否把逾3億美元訂單轉成實際交付與營收，是上市後的觀察重點。

news.Title: Amazon (AMZN) and Apple (AAPL) Must Face a UK Class Action Over Marketplace Sales
news.Content:
Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN ) and Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL ) were told on September 28 that part of a consumer class action against them can proceed, after a ruling by Britain's Competition Appeal Tribunal.

The claim concerns a 2018 arrangement that allegedly restricted which sellers could list Apple and Beats products on Amazon's UK marketplace. Amazon closed Monday at $246.15 and Apple at $338.40.

READ ALSO: Amazon (AMZN) Sued Again, This Time over How it Treats Pregnant Warehouse Workers

The Claim is Too Small to Matter to Either Company:

The surviving portion of the claim is valued at between £289 million and £306 million, including interest. Amazon is worth about $2.7 trillion and Apple close to $4.9 trillion. Even a total loss would not register in either company's results.

The tribunal narrowed the case considerably. Claims covering Apple products bought directly from Apple or from other retailers were thrown out, with the judge describing the reasoning behind them as a complex and speculative theory of harm.

So this is the smaller version of the case, brought on the second attempt after an earlier filing was refused last year over concerns about the proposed class representative and its funding.

DON'T MISS: Amazon (AMZN) Puts Another $1.9 Billion Into its Delivery Network. The Cost of the Last Mile is Rising

The Real Risk is to How Amazon Polices its Marketplace:

The claims the tribunal allowed through are the ones aimed at the marketplace itself. Judge Kelyn Bacon described them as "plausible, credible and grounded in the facts", which is a low bar for certification but not a meaningless one.

The allegation is simple. Two companies agreed on who could sell a product, and buyers paid more as a result. Amazon's marketplace is central to its economics. Third-party sellers pay fees, and advertising revenue attaches to those listings.

Any legal test of who Amazon may exclude from that marketplace, and on what terms, reaches further than one product category in one country.

Britain has also built a collective action regime that allows large consumer claims to be aggregated, and both companies have faced claims under it before. A ruling that lets one case proceed makes the next filing easier to bring.

Apple said it strongly disagrees with the claims. Certification only means the case will now be heard. The timing is awkward for Apple in one respect. It arrives days after a United States jury ordered the company to pay about $5.7 billion in an unrelated patent case, so the legal column is filling up even though neither matter threatens the business.

Story Continues

Conclusion:

The financial exposure here is negligible for two companies of this size, and the tribunal removed the larger part of the claim before letting the rest go forward. However, the part that survived goes to how Amazon governs its marketplace rather than to one distribution deal signed in 2018, and that is the question with a longer tail. Britain's collective action regime rewards claims that clear this stage, so the ruling matters less for what it costs and more for what it invites. Certification is not a finding of liability, and both companies will contest it, but the case now proceeds on the ground least comfortable for Amazon.

Market Sentiment:

Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) was held by 369 hedge funds with a combined stake value of about $97.1 billion at the end of Q2 2026 in the Insider Monkey database. This is up from 353 hedge fund holders with a cumulative investment value of around $77.6 billion in the previous quarter.

news.Title: 台股ETF「人氣、績效」兩樣情！ 00919吸8萬人 3檔雙料資優生出爐
news.Content: 集保戶股權分散統計最新出爐，截至9月24日，台股ETF人氣前10大排行大致維持穩定，不過在美國10年期公債殖利率走高、油價反彈及市場波動加劇下，投資人布局開始出現明顯分歧。統計顯示，人氣10天王中有4檔9月以來受益人數下滑，其餘6檔則逆勢增加，且每檔增幅均超過千人。值得注意的是，10檔ETF同期全數繳出正報酬，其中7檔更跑贏大盤4.11%，報酬率介於5.12%至7.27%。 009816、0050、00878「績效＋人氣」雙增 進一步交叉比較9月績效與受益人數，凱基台灣TOP50（009816）、元大台灣50（0050）及國泰永續高股息（00878）表現格外突出。009816於9月以來上漲6.49%，受益人數增加6325人；0050上漲5.79%，增加2572人；00878則上漲5.12%，受益人數增加5917人，3檔同時具備績效與人氣成長，被市場視為人氣、表現雙雙亮眼的ETF。 其中009816今年2月掛牌後規模快速成長，截至9月24日已逼近2000億元，受益人數達91.83萬人，成為市值型ETF市場受到關注的新兵。法人認為，在市場資金輪動加速之際，市值型與高股息ETF仍持續吸引投資人布局。 00981A、00403A漲得多卻「掉粉」 不過，ETF績效亮眼並不代表人氣同步成長。9月績效冠軍主動統一台股增長（00981A）上漲7.27%，卻出現受益人數減少2萬5961人的情況；主動統一升級50（00403A）同期上漲6.46%，受益人數更大減9萬908人，呈現「績效強、人氣降」的反差。 相較之下，高股息ETF吸金力道更為明顯。群益台灣精選高息（00919）9月以來受益人數大增8萬238人，是人氣10大ETF中增加最多；復華台灣科技優息（00929）及元大高股息（0056）受益人數也分別增加1萬3037人、1萬103人，顯示在市場震盪環境下，部分投資人仍偏好高股息題材。

news.Title: 〈台股盤後〉台積電尾盤急殺 4萬8得而復失 終場漲308點留上影線
news.Content:
台股今(30)日顯著回神，由電子權值股領軍反攻，面板雙虎更雙雙漲停，盤中一度飆漲748點，衝上48,379點，但隨著獲利了結賣壓出籠，台積電終場急殺，使得指數再度失守4萬8千點大關，留下上影線，但仍守住五日線，收在47,940.13點，上漲308.17點，成交量達8,756億元，較昨日放大。

news.Title: Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights: Tesla
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – September 30, 2026 – Today, Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights Tesla TSLA.

Another Roadster Delay -- But Tesla's Real Story Is Finally Turning

There is a running joke among Tesla watchers that the second-generation Roadster exists primarily as a rhetorical device.

Elon Musk rolled a prototype out from beneath a Semi trailer in November 2017, promised production by 2020, then spent the better part of a decade moving the date. At last November's shareholder meeting he floated a demonstration on April Fool's Day, cheerfully noting the date gave him "deniability because I can say I was just kidding."

On Monday, Tesla did it again. The reveal scheduled for this Thursday, October 1st in Waco, Texas has been pushed to October 15th.

So a measure of skepticism is thoroughly earned. Yet both the reason for this delay and the broader backdrop are more encouraging than the headline suggests — and the nearer-term catalyst is no longer the Roadster at all.

The Excuse Is Also a Disclosure

Tesla's explanation was specific: "We've been tracking the weather closely with local meteorologists, but given the severe conditions predicted and because this event can only be held outdoors, we've made the difficult decision to reschedule."

That phrase — "can only be held outdoors" — is the most revealing thing Tesla has said about this car in years. Vehicle unveilings happen indoors all the time. An event that physically cannot be held under a roof implies a demonstration requiring open air and considerable clearance, which lines up precisely with the four bright thruster plumes in Tesla's teaser image and with the SpaceX-derived cold-gas thruster package Musk has described for years.

Reports have suggested the car may briefly leave the ground under remote operation, with spectators held hundreds of yards back because the thrusters are loud enough to risk hearing damage. The FAA had restricted aircraft and drone flights over the area through October 2nd.

In other words, Tesla just indirectly confirmed that the demonstration is what the rumor mill said it was. That is not nothing after nine years of vagueness.

There is a second, harder signal. Tesla has reopened Roadster reservations, and the terms are serious: a $50,000 deposit — $5,000 by credit card followed by a $45,000 wire transfer — with $250,000 required for the Founders Series. Companies do not collect wire transfers of that size for vehicles they have no intention of building.

The Nearer Catalyst Is Friday

Story Continues

With the reveal pushed to October 15th, the more immediate event is Tesla's third-quarter delivery report, due this Friday — and the setup there is genuinely interesting.

Wall Street consensus sits near 454,000 vehicles, but the dispersion is extraordinary: estimates run from roughly 422,000 at the low end to 482,000 at the high, a 60,000-unit spread. Goldman Sachs is at 435,000 after cutting from 490,000. Prediction markets on Kalshi have been running around 480,000.

The Street's recent track record here is poor. Tesla's company-compiled consensus for the second quarter was 406,024 deliveries. The actual figure came in at 480,126 — a beat of 74,000 units, with Kalshi traders landing almost exactly right. When professional forecasters have been that wrong that recently, and estimates have been cut aggressively into the print, the bar is low. Analysts suggest a figure above 485,000 would constitute a real upside surprise.

The Shift That Actually Matters

Here is the development that best supports a constructive view, and it has nothing to do with the Roadster.

Earlier this month, Goldman Sachs cut its third-quarter delivery forecast by 55,000 units, citing softness in China, the United States and Europe. Not long ago, a reduction of that size from a bank of that influence would have sent the shares sharply lower.

It barely moved.

That non-reaction tells you the market has stopped valuing Tesla primarily on how many cars it sells. Investors have repriced the company around autonomy, robotics and energy. Whether that framework is correct is debatable — the car business still funds everything else. But it means the delivery weakness that has weighed on sentiment all year is losing its power over the stock, and that removes the single largest overhang on the shares.

What's Actually Working

Beneath the margin noise, the second quarter delivered real operational progress. Robotaxi service now operates in seven U.S. markets, with Nevada approving fleet expansion to as many as 5,000 vehicles. Cybercab production has begun at Gigafactory Texas. Full Self-Driving subscriptions reached 1.48 million, up 56% year over year, with attach rates near 55% of new North American deliveries. Musk has said robotaxi miles are growing more than 10% per week.

Beyond that: an Optimus production line at Fremont, Semi commissioning in Nevada, Megapack 3 arriving for 2026, a significant Semi order recently booked, and a potential European approval of unsupervised FSD that would represent a major regulatory unlock.

Bottom Line

Tesla spent most of 2026 being judged on the one metric it can no longer easily grow — quarterly car deliveries — while the businesses meant to justify its valuation remained promises. That equation is finally shifting. Robotaxi is live in seven cities, Cybercab is in production, FSD adoption is compounding, and the market has demonstrably stopped punishing delivery cuts.

The Roadster slipping two weeks is an annoyance, not a thesis-breaker. If anything, a company that reschedules rather than stages a compromised indoor version of an event it has promised for nine years is behaving like one that intends to deliver something worth watching.

news.Title: Apple iPhone 18 Pro sales rise 12% in China launch week - Counterpoint
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Apple's iPhone 18 Pro series sales in China rose 12% year-over-year in the first week of launch, helping the company take the top spot in the country's smartphone market, according to Counterpoint Research.

Still guessing which names to buy? Our AI rebuilds its stock picks at the start of every month. The list is beating the market by 120%. See what's on it »

Apple accounted for 33% of China's smartphone sales in Week 38, which covered September 14-20, even though the iPhone 18 Pro series was on sale for only the final three days of the week, Counterpoint said in a report published on Wednesday.

The research firm said China's weekly smartphone sales have fallen at a double-digit annual rate since July as soft consumer demand and higher memory costs weighed on the market. September's new product launches are expected to support a sequential recovery.

Should you buy NVIDIA right now? Before you decide, consider this: an AI-powered list of stock picks is outperforming the market by 120%, and it updates at the start of every month. See this month's picks »

Counterpoint Senior Analyst Ivan Lam said the delayed launch of the standard iPhone 18 may have encouraged some consumers to move up to the Pro models. At the same time, price increases of more than $200 across many Chinese flagship phones may have improved the iPhone Pro's relative value proposition.

Apple's strong launch came as Chinese smartphone makers also introduced new flagship models ahead of the country's National Day holiday. Rising memory costs have pushed up prices for higher-memory versions and phones using 2-nanometer chips, which could weigh on sales later in the year.

Counterpoint expects the latest generation of Chinese flagship models to record lower fourth-quarter sales than their predecessors.

Huawei has introduced the Pura X View, a wide-screen slab phone with a 16:9.5 display ratio aimed at consumers seeking a larger screen without the cost or bulk of a foldable, Counterpoint said. Its pricing and flagship specifications have supported strong initial sales.

Despite Apple's strong Pro launch, the broader Chinese smartphone market remained weak, with Week 38 sales still 17% below the comparable 2025 week, according to Counterpoint's tracker.

news.Title: Zuckerberg lost $8.9 billion in a day as Meta's AI rally cracked: his net worth fell from $266.4 billion to $257.5 billion as Meta shares dropped about 4% to $749.26 after Goldman Sachs warned AI spenders need about $300 billion a year in AI revenue just to break even.
news.Content:
A fortune built on stock can grow by billions before lunch and give a chunk of it back before the closing bell. That's the trade-off that comes with owning a company instead of drawing a paycheck.

You don't need a billion dollars to feel it. If you own an S&P 500 index fund or a target-date fund in your 401(k), you already hold small slices of the tech giants now spending hundreds of billions of dollars on artificial intelligence.

For most of September, those slices looked like a gift. Meta Platforms (META) rallied roughly 36% in the month after launching Muse, its personal AI assistant, and came within one percent of a $2 trillion market value on Sept. 24.

Then one Wall Street note asked the question every AI investor eventually has to face. When does all this spending pay for itself?

Meta founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg found out what that question costs on Sept. 25. His estimated net worth fell $8.9 billion in a single session, the biggest one-day loss of any billionaire that day, according to Forbes .

Meta's capital spending bill keeps climbing

Meta is one of the biggest spenders in the AI race. The company expects 2026 capital expenditures, including finance lease payments, of $130 billion to $145 billion, according to Meta's second-quarter earnings release .

Related: Zuckerberg's stock rebound made him world's 5th richest at $222B

The quarter itself showed the strain. Meta booked $60.8 billion in revenue, up 28% year over year, while spending $31.08 billion on capital projects in those three months alone.

Free cash flow, the cash left after those investments, shrank to $784 million from $8.55 billion a year earlier, CNBC reported.

In my analysis, that is the number that matters most if you hold Meta in a retirement account. Revenue shows demand, while free cash flow shows whether a business can fund its bets without leaning on its balance sheet.

Muse gave investors a reason to look past that squeeze. The app logged 2.8 million downloads within two weeks of launch and overtook ChatGPT as the top free app in the U.S. and Canada, according to Sensor Tower data cited by Reuters .

Related: Mark Zuckerberg and Nvidia CEO weigh in on Anthropic AI proposal

"Meta has really found lightning in a bottle here," Michael O'Rourke, chief market strategist at JonesTrading, told Reuters .

That enthusiasm peaked on Sept. 24, when Meta closed at $777.59, its highest close of the year, and Zuckerberg's fortune reached $266.4 billion, according to Forbes . Three days earlier, a single session had added about $25 billion to his net worth.

Story Continues

Goldman Sachs puts a $300 billion hurdle on AI payback

The reversal traced back to a Goldman Sachs (GS) strategy note. Strategist Ryan Hammond estimated that the largest U.S. AI spenders need about $300 billion a year in AI revenue just to break even on their investments, Investing.com reported.

Baird's strong agentic Al call on Micron is spot on

To earn solid returns, annual spending on AI applications would need to reach roughly $1 trillion, the firm estimated, Benzinga reported.

The scale of the bet explains the nerves. Hammond put 2026 capital spending by the biggest cloud and AI companies at roughly $800 billion, with Wall Street consensus expecting about $1.1 trillion in 2027, Investing.com reported.

Goldman did flag real progress. Cloud revenue at those companies ran at an annualized pace roughly $70 billion above its pre-AI trend in the second quarter, and their announced backlogs top $1.5 trillion, Yahoo Finance reported.

Still, $70 billion is less than a quarter of the $300 billion bar. That gap is what traders sold on Sept. 25.

Goldman told clients to watch the companies buying AI services for proof. "The impact of AI on corporate earnings should become increasingly visible in coming quarters," Goldman wrote, according to The Motley Fool .

Meta had a second headwind that afternoon. A New Mexico jury found that the company misled state residents in a case tied to the Cambridge Analytica data scandal, Reuters reported, and a Meta spokesperson said the company disagreed with the verdict.

Zuckerberg's losing day by the numbers

Here's how the day broke down, according to Forbes real-time data.

Net worth : $257.5 billion as of 2:30 p.m. ET on Sept. 25, down $8.9 billion.

Day before : $266.4 billion at the Sept. 24 close.

Meta stock : down about four percent to $749.26.

Ranking : No. 6, down from No. 4 at the Sept. 24 close.

Stake : Zuckerberg owns about 13% of Meta.

Next-largest loss that day : Larry Ellison, down $1.6 billion.

Index fund investors felt the reversal too

Zuckerberg's loss is paper wealth, since most of his fortune sits in Meta stock. Your exposure works the same way, just on a smaller scale.

Meta sits inside most broad U.S. stock index funds, alongside Microsoft (MSFT), Alphabet (GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN) and Oracle (ORCL), the peers Forbes said Goldman named in its note.

Related: Michael Dell jumped past Zuckerberg and Brin to No. 4 richest: his fortune rose more than $11 billion in a day to $276.4 billion as Dell Technologies stock climbed 6% to $570.72 on a $95 billion AI server backlog

That concentration cuts both ways. When the AI trade runs, your balance rises with it, and when a major bank questions the payoff, those holdings can fall together.

I'd use Sept. 25 as a stress test for your own account. Check how much of your 401(k) now sits in large-cap growth or tech funds after this year's run.

If a handful of AI spenders now make up more of your account than you planned, rebalancing back to your target mix locks in some gains while keeping you in the trade.

Third-quarter earnings become the next test for Muse

Meta's next checkpoint is its third-quarter report, when investors will see whether Muse is showing up in revenue. The company has guided third-quarter revenue to $61 billion to $64 billion.

Related: Mark Zuckerberg says Meta found a way to make more money

Truist Securities estimates Muse could add at least $28.5 billion in annual revenue by fiscal 2030, Reuters reported.

Even that bullish estimate is less than a tenth of Goldman's break-even bar for the group. The AI boom may still pay off, but Sept. 25 showed that investors now want receipts to go with the downloads.

For your money, the lesson is practical. Own the AI story if you believe in it, and size it so a billionaire's $9 billion day never becomes a hole in your retirement plan.

news.Title: MongoDB Unveils AI Products, Raises Long-Term Targets Amid CEO Transition
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in MongoDB, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Leadership transition: MongoDB's former CEO resigned to join Meta, with former CEO Dev Ittycheria serving as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor. Management expects business operations to continue normally.

AI product expansion: MongoDB launched Atlas Infinite, which separates compute and storage for elastic agent-driven workloads, and Atlas Agent Engine, which provides persistent memory, security, governance and runtime capabilities for AI agents.

Higher long-term targets: The company now targets more than 20% total revenue growth, mid-20% Atlas growth, expanding operating margins and 80%–100% free-cash-flow conversion over three years. MongoDB also authorized an additional $1 billion share-repurchase plan .

MongoDB Stock Drops 17% After CEO Exit—What Investors Should Know

MongoDB (NASDAQ:MDB) used its 2026 Investor Day to outline a leadership transition, new AI-focused product launches and updated long-term financial targets, with executives emphasizing continued investment in enterprise sales, partnerships and application modernization.

Chief Financial Officer Mike Berry said former CEO CJ resigned last Friday to take a role at Meta, and the board named former longtime CEO Dev Ittycheria as interim president and CEO while it searches for a permanent successor. Berry said the company expects "business as usual" during the transition and described MongoDB as being supported by a broader management team rather than any one individual.

→ 5 Scary-Good Stocks With Strong October Catalysts and Breakout Potential

MarketBeat Week in Review – 09/07 - 09/11

Ittycheria said the board has already begun its CEO search and that the company is seeking a leader with experience building software companies and understanding both technology and go-to-market execution. He said his immediate priorities are sustaining business momentum, sharpening product and sales execution, and supporting MongoDB's culture.

AI Strategy Centers on Data, Scale and Flexibility

Ittycheria framed MongoDB's strategy as an effort to become an "intelligent data platform," arguing that AI and agentic applications need fresh operational data, precise retrieval, elastic scaling, state management and governance. He said AI represents a tailwind for the company because it can create more software workloads, introduce new workloads involving agents and memory, and expand MongoDB's customer base among AI-native companies and frontier labs.

Story Continues

→ Akamai's Anthropic Deal Puts $5.5 Billion Behind Its Edge AI Pivot

Could Snowflake's Big Quarter Be a Sign of More to Come?

The company cited its JSON document model, retrieval capabilities, security tools and ability to run across cloud and self-managed environments as differentiators. Ittycheria said customers are increasingly selective about where AI workloads run because of intellectual-property protection, data residency and sovereignty concerns.

Ben Cefalo, MongoDB's chief product officer for core products, said the company is continuing to invest in Enterprise Advanced, its self-managed offering, alongside the Atlas cloud service. He said customers in regulated industries and geographies with specific data requirements need deployment flexibility, while companies also want protection against dependence on a single environment.

→ 2 Cybersecurity Stocks Breaking Out as AI Continues to Be a Tailwind

Cefalo said MongoDB 9.0 delivers performance improvements including up to 20% higher transactional throughput, 35% faster reads, 30% faster updates and twice the throughput on larger instances. The release also expands the company's Queryable Encryption capability, which allows customers to query encrypted data while retaining encryption of the data and query.

Atlas Infinite and Agent Engine Announced

MongoDB also introduced Atlas Infinite, a new Atlas deployment option that separates compute from storage. Cefalo said the architecture is designed to handle bursty and unpredictable agent-driven workloads by allowing compute and storage to scale independently. Atlas Infinite is in public preview on AWS, according to management, while the existing Atlas offering is being renamed Atlas Core Database.

The company said Atlas Infinite has been in private preview with customers including Icon Solutions, PicPay and Carrier. Cefalo said the offering is intended to support elastic scaling, tunable performance and reduced capacity-planning complexity, though it is not a separate database requiring application code changes.

Pablo Stern-Plaza, chief product officer for AI and emerging products, announced Atlas Agent Engine, an agentic infrastructure product that combines persistent memory, security guardrails, governance and runtime capabilities. The offering is designed to work across clouds, models, frameworks and data sources, management said.

Stern-Plaza said Agent Engine is available to existing Atlas customers through public preview. He said the product can create monetization opportunities through agent runtime and memory services while also driving Atlas consumption. Management expects the product to become generally available later in the current fiscal year or early in the following year.

Citizens Bank SVP and Head of Data Platform Vikas Agarwal said the bank is using MongoDB Atlas for tier-one applications and is exploring multi-agent systems for platform resiliency and issue identification. He said the Agent Engine memory capabilities, flexible model choices and security features were particularly relevant for the bank's use cases.

Go-to-Market and Partnership Investment

Chief Revenue Officer Ryan Mac Ban said MongoDB plans to increase its focus on enterprise executive buyers, AI and digital-native customers, product specialization and application modernization. The company is also targeting growth in U.S. federal, Asia-Pacific and Japan markets, he said.

Mac Ban said MongoDB's application modernization platform, combined with AI tooling and partners such as Cognition, is intended to reduce the cost and time required to migrate legacy Oracle, SQL and relational workloads. Ittycheria said advances in AI model capability have improved the viability of modernization initiatives that had previously been difficult because rewriting application logic was complex.

Chief Customer Officer Erica Volini said the company is expanding its partner ecosystem across coding agents, AI platforms, systems integrators, hyperscalers, neoclouds and independent software vendors. She said roughly half of MongoDB revenue is supported by a hyperscaler partner and marketplace revenue is growing faster than overall revenue year over year.

Updated Financial Targets

Berry said MongoDB met or exceeded the commitments it outlined at its prior investor day. Atlas revenue grew about 29% in fiscal 2026, while the company's fiscal 2027 guidance calls for approximately 27% Atlas growth. Enterprise Advanced and other revenue grew 7% in fiscal 2026, and the fiscal 2027 outlook implies 11% growth.

For the longer term, MongoDB shortened its target horizon from three-to-five years to three years and raised several growth objectives:

Total revenue growth of more than 20%.

Atlas revenue growth in the mid-20% range.

Enterprise Advanced and other ARR growth of more than 10%.

Annual non-GAAP operating-margin expansion of 100 to 200 basis points.

Free-cash-flow conversion of 80% to 100% of non-GAAP operating income.

Berry said MongoDB expects to remain GAAP profitable beyond fiscal 2027 and aims to approach a Rule of 50 profile by the end of the three-year period, though he did not formally commit to that outcome. He also said the board approved an additional $1 billion for the company's share-repurchase plan.

Management said AI-native and frontier-lab customers account for roughly 3% to 5% of Atlas revenue, but that revenue from the cohort grew 165% year over year. Berry said the company views the segment as small but rapidly expanding, while its larger enterprise customers continue to be a major source of expansion, cross-selling and new workload adoption.

About MongoDB (NASDAQ:MDB)

MongoDB, Inc develops and provides a general-purpose, document-oriented database platform. Its technology is designed to help organizations store, manage and analyze structured and unstructured data for applications such as artificial intelligence, analytics, mobile services, e-commerce and enterprise software.

The company's principal offering is MongoDB Atlas, a fully managed cloud database service available across major cloud infrastructure providers. MongoDB also offers Enterprise Advanced, which provides commercial database software, security, operational controls and support for organizations running databases in their own environments or across hybrid and multicloud infrastructures.

news.Title: Mark Zuckerberg sends bold message to Meta investors after Muse
news.Content:
While the internet argued over whether Meta's new Muse AI agent could rival ChatGPT, the company quietly revealed something else entirely.

A cable stretching 4,300 miles under the Atlantic Ocean, built to move more data per second than any transoceanic line in history.

The project barely registered outside industry circles. But it says more about where Meta (META) thinks its real advantage lies than any single product launch could. It fits into a pattern the company has been building for years without much public attention.

What is Meta's Petal cable ?

Meta announced Petal on Sept. 21, describing it as the first transoceanic subsea cable capable of delivering a full petabit per second of capacity, connecting the United States directly to France's Atlantic coast over roughly 7,000 kilometers, or about 4,300 miles.

The company is not building it alone. Meta is partnering with NEC as the turnkey system supplier and Sumitomo Electric Industries for the fiber technology, while French telecom Orange will manage the cable's landing on France's Atlantic coast.

More Mark Zuckerberg:

Mark Zuckerberg, Microsoft CEO just made major AI decision

Zuckerberg's stock rebound made him world's 5th richest at $222B

Mark Zuckerberg backs Elon Musk Silicon Valley decision

The technical leap is real. Petal will be the first system to deploy multi-core fiber technology at transoceanic distances. Its two-core fiber design uses 48 pairs of spatial channels, doubling the capacity of Anjana, Meta's previous 24 fiber-pair system, without a proportional increase in power or physical cable size, Meta's engineering team wrote .

Meta already has experience building at this scale. The company worked with Microsoft, Aqua Comms, and Vodafone to complete the Amitié cable system in 2023. That was a 16-fiber-pair transatlantic system delivering up to 400 terabits per second, the highest-capacity transoceanic cable ever deployed at the time, Computer Weekly reported .

Why Meta is building its own ocean cables

For years, tech companies simply rented capacity on cables built and operated by telecom carriers. But the explosive growth of cloud and AI traffic is pushing the largest technology companies toward greater direct control of the infrastructure carrying their data.

Meta has quietly become one of the largest investors in the industry. The company has been involved in more than 20 undersea cable projects over the past decade. It has progressively taken a larger role in building and controlling the physical infrastructure that carries its global traffic.

Story Continues

Petal is only one piece of a much larger buildout. It sits alongside Project Waterworth, Meta's more than 31,000-mile cable system spanning five continents. Together, the projects form part of Meta's broader effort to build out its global subsea infrastructure, TechCrunch reported .

The logic behind Meta's infrastructure push extends beyond subsea cables.

The company's Hyperion campus in Louisiana crossed $50 billion in committed investment this year. That reflects Meta's broader effort to secure greater control over the physical infrastructure needed to scale AI, according to CNBC .

The bigger AI infrastructure bill behind it

Petal and Waterworth are expensive additions to an already enormous spending plan. Meta narrowed its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $130 billion to $145 billion, up from a prior range of $125 billion to $145 billion.

The company cited continued heavy investment in data-center capacity and other infrastructure needed to support future growth, CNBC reported .

That spending has already squeezed Meta's cash generation. The company produced just $784 million in free cash flow during the second quarter, down sharply from $8.55 billion in the same quarter a year earlier. Infrastructure spending consumed most of the cash produced by operations.

Meta's spending is part of a nationwide pattern that dwarfs previous infrastructure booms. A Brookings Institution analysis put the total cost of AI buildout projects at $10.3 trillion from 2025 to 2032.

That is a larger economic investment than the major U.S. canal, electrification, railroad, highway, and telecommunications booms combined, Quartz reported .

That scale of spending has not gone unnoticed by local communities. Meta's own CFO Susan Li described the AI infrastructure building environment as dynamic and uncertain on a recent earnings call. Opposition to large data-center projects has grown in several U.S. communities.

Meta has said it invested more than $2.3 billion in Ohio data centers alone since 2018, paying more than $40 million in property taxes and fees during that time, according to Stocktwits .

What Petal means for Meta investors

Owning cables and data centers outright only makes sense if Meta's AI ambitions actually require that much dedicated infrastructure. The company has said it remains constrained by available computing capacity today, suggesting the buildout is not simply precautionary.

Financing that scale of investment is also drawing more scrutiny from lenders. Banks have started weighing community support and project readiness more heavily before financing AI-related infrastructure. That shift could make the broader AI infrastructure buildout more expensive or complicated to finance.

The cable announcement is easy to overlook next to a flashy AI agent launch. But it may say more about Meta's actual strategy than Muse does.

The company is increasingly treating control of the physical infrastructure connecting its data centers as a strategic requirement for scaling its AI systems. That strategy will face a major test as Petal enters service in 2029.

news.Title: How much AMZN stock does Amazon’s founder Jeff Bezos actually own?
news.Content:
Long before Jeff Bezos became the second-richest man on the planet, light years before he served looks as an unlikely style icon , and decades before he hosted a foam party on his $500 million superyacht, Koru , Bezos was just a regular guy with a dream, starting a small business out of a Bellevue, Washington garage .

Within a month of launching his online bookstore, however, Amazon (AMZN), then known as Cadabra, had shipped books to all 50 states and 45 countries . Amazon was growing—fast. Bezos would eventually describe its growth model as a "flywheel," where lower prices generated more customers, increased traffic attracted more sellers, and greater scale allowed Amazon to reduce prices even further. Just four years after Bezos launched Amazon, his company had grown into the world's largest online retailer .

But while Bezos controlled 100% ownership of Amazon when he founded it in 1994, he diluted his ownership in order to raise the capital it needed to fuel even greater growth. In 1995, Bezos raised $1 million in seed capital by selling 20% in the company to a cohort of angel investors that included his parents, his brother, and his sister. By the time Amazon made its IPO on May 15, 1997, Bezos owned roughly 43% of the company. After his 2019 divorce from MacKenzie Scott, Bezos' stake fell to roughly 12% (Scott received about 4% of Amazon's outstanding shares in the divorce settlement). By the end of 2021, after Bezos had stepped down from the role of Amazon CEO, his stake was 12.7%.

Today, Amazon's CEO is Andrew Jassy, Bezos' top adviser and former head of Amazon Web Services. But while Bezos is no longer responsible for the company's day-to-day operations, he continues to be Amazon's largest shareholder.

How much of AMZN does Jeff Bezos own?

As of Amazon's May 2026 proxy statement , Jeff Bezos owned 950 million shares, equating to about 8.8% of the company.

However, he has since sold and donated millions of shares. According to Bezos' latest SEC filing , he owned approximately 879.3 million Amazon shares as of Aug. 26, 2026. Those shares were worth $219.2 billion as of Amazon's September 2026 share price of $249.27.

Amazon is not Bezos' only major asset. He also owns The Washington Post , aerospace company Blue Origin, and his private investment firm, Bezos Expeditions. He and his second wife, Lauren Sánchez Bezos, also hold a multimillion-dollar real estate portfolio that includes properties in Miami, Beverly Hills, New York, Washington, DC, and Maui.

Is Jeff Bezos the largest individual shareholder of Amazon?

Story Continues

Yes, Bezos remains Amazon's largest individual shareholder. Current CEO Andrew Jassy holds roughly 2.25 million shares , or a 0.02% stake in the business, worth approximately $562.3 million.

More on founder's wealth:

Steve Jobs' net worth: How rich Apple's founder could have been

Warren Buffett's net worth: A look at his fortune in retirement

Mark Zuckerberg's net worth: How the Facebook founder hit $200 billion

Douglas Herrington, Amazon's CEO of Worldwide Stores and Shelley Reynolds, Amazon's VP and Principal Accounting Officer, both own less than a 0.01% stake of shares outstanding. Herrington holds 474,638 shares roughly valued at $118.3 million, while Reynolds holds 119,780 shares valued at $29.9 million.

Amazon's largest institutional shareholders

Institutional investors also hold significant stakes in Amazon. According to 13F filings for the quarter ending June 30, 2026, BlackRock held approximately 748.4 million Amazon shares, while Vanguard Capital Management and State Street held approximately 635.7 million shares and 397.2 million shares, respectively.

news.Title: History Says Nvidia's Record $150 Billion Buyback Is Good News for the Stock
news.Content:
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) said on Monday, Sept. 28, that its board added $150 billion to the company's share repurchase authorization, taking the amount left to $235 billion. The chipmaker called it the biggest boost to a buyback authorization in history. It beats the $110 billion Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) approved in 2024.

Investors liked the news. Shares gained about 2% on Monday as I write, trading near $230.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

And history suggests they might have reason to. Apple's biggest buyback authorizations from 2018 through 2025 and Nvidia's own increases from 2023 through 2025 were each followed by a gain in the stock over the next 12 months. In eight of these nine cases, the stock beat the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC).

But I think the cash behind those buybacks did more of that work than the buybacks themselves.

Image source Getty Images.

A record authorization

With around 24.1 billion shares outstanding, Nvidia is worth about $5.5 trillion at around $230 a share. The full $235 billion would buy back a bit over 4% of the company.

Nvidia expects to spend the total remaining amount through fiscal 2028, which ends in January 2028 -- more than $40 billion a quarter over the roughly 16 months left.

That would more than double the current rate. Nvidia's buybacks have already risen, from $9.7 billion a year before to around $20 billion in each of the past two quarters.

Free cash flow for fiscal 2027's first half was $69.9 billion, 77% higher than a year before, or around $35 billion a quarter.

In other words, management is counting on lots more cash. CEO Jensen Huang linked the move to the company's "cash generation" in the announcement.

The stocks usually beat the market

Apple approved buyback authorizations of $90 billion or more in 2018, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025. (Its $100 billion authorization this April, like Nvidia's $80 billion boost in May, is too new to judge.) Measured from the close on each announcement day to a year later, Apple stock gained in all six periods and beat the S&P 500 in five.

The gaps were often wide. After the $100 billion authorization in May 2018, Apple shares climbed around 24% while the index rose about 10%. And after the $90 billion increase in April 2021, the stock gained over 22% versus about 2% for the index.

Story Continues

Nvidia's own record is even better.

Its board added $25 billion in August 2023, $50 billion in August 2024 and $60 billion in August 2025. Over the 12 months after each, the stock rose about 175%, 43% and 26%, respectively, versus gains of about 27%, 16% and 19% for the S&P 500.

Some of these wins were narrow, though. Apple beat the index by only about 2 percentage points after its 2025 authorization. And Nvidia's 2025 lead hinged on the last day of the window, when shares jumped after its next earnings report.

Is the buyback the reason?

Probably not on its own. After all, boards tend to approve big buybacks when cash is rolling in, and those gains likely came from the businesses making that cash.

Apple's only miss came after it announced a $90 billion authorization in May 2023, when its sales were shrinking. Apple's revenue for fiscal 2023, which ended Sept. 30, 2023, dropped 3%, and it was still down 4% year over year in the March 2024 quarter. Over the 12 months after the announcement, Apple shares rose about 11% while the S&P 500 gained about 26%.

Nvidia shows the other side. Its diluted share count for the fiscal second quarter of 2027, which ended July 26, 2026, was only about 1% smaller than a year before, despite almost $40 billion of buybacks over the fiscal year's first half. Earnings per share, meanwhile, more than doubled. At a company this big, buybacks change per-share results only a little.

Is the record buyback good news for Nvidia stock, then? I think it is, mainly because of what it says about the cash coming. Roughly doubling the buyback rate only makes sense if management expects free cash flow to keep rising.

Of course, Nvidia's stock may still trail the market over the next year. If artificial intelligence (AI) spending cools, that cash might fall short, and Nvidia doesn't have to use the full authorization.

But the price helps. Shares trade at around 15 times Nvidia's expected fiscal 2028 earnings, while Apple trades at about 36 times its expected earnings in fiscal 2027, which ends next September. Every dollar Nvidia spends on its own stock buys over twice the expected earnings that a dollar of Apple's buybacks does.

I'd consider buying the stock alongside the company at this price.

news.Title: NVIDIA Just Turned AI Safety Into a Spending Story and These 3 Stocks Benefit
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Marvell Technology, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

NVIDIA's Open Agent Safety Platform and industry self-regulation could increase AI infrastructure spending by requiring more testing, monitoring and inference computing power.

Analyst Luke Lango highlights Marvell Technology, Arm Holdings and Lumentum Holdings as beneficiaries of a shift from GPU-heavy training toward inference, connectivity and bandwidth demand.

All three stocks depend on continuous model testing and serving rather than frontier AI progress, though rising bond yields and tight liquidity could still pressure their valuations.

NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) spent most of September arguing that AI safety is an engineering problem, not a legal one. On Sept. 28, the company shipped the product to prove it. NVIDIA introduced the Open Agent Safety Platform alongside more than 100 industry partners, pairing open-source access controls with an independent monitoring layer that runs on separate silicon so it can watch an AI agent without living inside it. Jensen Huang framed the launch plainly: AI's potential only gets realized if safety gets solved alongside capability.

Investors hear "safety" and price in a slowdown. Luke Lango of InvestorPlace thinks that reading is backward and that a self-regulation path widens the AI infrastructure spending pipeline rather than narrowing it. That's the setup behind three names he's watching.

→ AST SpaceMobile's New Securities Lawsuit Adds Fuel to an Already Volatile Stock

Self-Regulation Costs More Compute, Not Less

Lango's argument starts with mechanics. If labs agree to evaluate each other's models rather than wait for Washington, every new release triggers another round of testing, monitoring and peer review. All of that runs on hardware.

It also changes the kind of hardware in demand. Slowing the frontier means slowing pre-training, the GPU-heavy part of the stack. Testing and serving models at scale is inference, and it depends less on raw chip power than on moving data efficiently and coordinating many tasks at once. Lango expects that shift from training to inference to define the next six to 12 months of demand, favoring CPUs and connectivity over raw accelerators.

→ Akamai's Anthropic Deal Puts $5.5 Billion Behind Its Edge AI Pivot

That's the tension worth watching. Under a safety regime, the AI trade doesn't die. It rotates.

Marvell Technology Sits Where the Bottleneck Moved

Huang made this case himself. At Computex in early June, he called Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) the next trillion-dollar company, pointing to the connectivity that lets thousands of chips behave like one machine.

Story Continues

→ Why 3 Struggling Stocks Are Suddenly Spending Big on Buybacks

Shares jumped more than 32% the next session, the stock's best day on record.

The business has kept pace with the rhetoric. Marvell guided fiscal 2027 revenue to roughly $12 billion and fiscal 2028 to about $18 billion, and the stock has returned over 200% so far in 2026.

It's also well off its highs, trading around 20% below its 52-week peak after an August sell-off. Lango treats that gap as the opportunity, arguing the data center networking names that ran hard, pulled back and held their long-term trend lines are where the shopping list starts.

Arm Holdings Is Selling CPUs Into a CPU Shortage

The second name is Arm Holdings (NASDAQ: ARM), and the pitch is timing.

In March, Arm shipped the AGI CPU, the first production chip in its 35-year history as a licensing business. It runs up to 136 Neoverse V3 cores, is manufactured by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM) on a 3-nanometer node, and Arm claims more than double the performance per rack versus x86 platforms.

Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META) co-developed the chip and took first delivery, with OpenAI, Cerebras (NASDAQ: CBRS) and Cloudflare (NYSE: NET) among launch partners.

The CPU went from afterthought to orchestration layer as agentic workloads spread. That resurgence has already carried Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) up roughly 280% over the past year and put a fresh bid under Intel (NASDAQ: INTC). Lango sees Arm as the higher-torque version of the same trade, because it's converting from royalties into silicon revenue right as AI inference demand accelerates.

Lumentum Holds the Bandwidth Bottleneck

Copper can only carry so much. As GPUs multiply and constantly talk to one another, data centers are swapping copper interconnects for optics, photonics and fiber. That's the core business of Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ: LITE).

The numbers reflect it. Lumentum closed fiscal 2026 with $1.01 billion in fourth-quarter revenue and guided the current quarter to a midpoint near $1.25 billion.

NVIDIA committed $2 billion to expand Lumentum's capacity and deepen joint development on data center optics.

Unlike Marvell and Arm, this stock hasn't corrected so much as stalled.

Lango reads the sideways action as consolidation ahead of a move rather than a broken growth story, and the AI safety stocks framing gives it a second tailwind: more model-checking means more traffic between chips, and more traffic means wider optical highways.

Self-Regulation Keeps the Capital Spending Cycle Intact

Marvell, Arm and Lumentum are three pieces of one machine: custom silicon, orchestration and bandwidth. None of them depends on the frontier labs racing faster. They depend on models being served, tested and checked constantly, which is precisely what self-regulation would institutionalize.

What the setup does depend on is CapEx discipline holding and the macro backdrop easing enough for high-multiple hardware names to re-rate. If the 10-year yield stays elevated and liquidity stays tight, good numbers may keep getting offset by a shrinking multiple, exactly as they have been.

Stay focused on where the marginal compute dollar goes, because that is what moves these stocks far more than the next doomsday headline.

For more on the physical AI wave and the infrastructure Elon Musk is assembling around it, see Luke Lango's special reports on Elon Musk, SpaceX and the next stage of AI.

Cathie Wood, CEO of Ark Invest, believes robotaxis will one day be a $10 trillion global industry. A survey of experts by McKinsey & Co., meanwhile, estimates that "the global rollout of robotaxis is now expected to become reality at a large scale in 2030." The consultancy stresses that "robotaxis will be the first commercial application for L4 in mobility -- not privately owned cars."

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Much of Tesla 's (NASDAQ: TSLA) $1.2 trillion valuation is now tied up in robotaxi growth opportunities. Shares trade at 13 times sales.

Uber Technologies (NYSE: UBER), meanwhile, trades below 3 times sales, with a market cap of around $140 billion. The market fears that the robotaxi revolution will disrupt Uber's core business. In reality, there's a good chance Uber will become the go-to platform for robotaxis worldwide.

Here's why Uber will win the robotaxi revolution

Pershing Square founder Bill Ackman recently summed up how powerful Uber has become in the ridesharing business. "Uber has achieved the rare feat of becoming a verb," he told Fortune in August.

This is key to Uber's ability to compete in a robotaxi-dominated world. The company already controls the demand side of the equation. Its Uber One membership has more than 50 million subscribers.

Tesla may be able to produce robotaxis more cheaply than the competition. But it still needs to convince consumers to download its app and then commit themselves to a Tesla-only service.

Uber, meanwhile, will be manufacturer-agnostic. Other robotaxi fleets, which will rely on high use rates to generate profits, will want to go where the demand is. That will mean participating in Uber's platform.

With free cash flow margins of nearly 20%, Uber stock is already cheap. And its future is much brighter than the bears would have you believe.

news.Title: Nancy Pelosi And Bill Ackman Are Betting On The Same Two Stocks
news.Content:
Uber (NYSE:UBER) and Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) are showing up in both Nancy Pelosi's trading disclosures and Bill Ackman's Pershing Square portfolio.

Pelosi's spouse bought 200 call options on Uber (NYSE:UBER) on May 29, with a $50 strike price expiring March 19, 2027. Bill Ackman's Pershing Square holds a much bigger position in the same stock. The fund's second-quarter 13F filing shows it owns 34.3 million Uber (NYSE:UBER) shares worth roughly $2.48 billion, making it the largest holding in the portfolio at 12.72% of assets. Ackman grew this stake by 15% during the quarter, adding to a position he first opened in early 2025.

Don't Miss: Can Uber's (UBER) Economic Moat Survive the Rise of Robotaxis?

Pelosi also holds Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) call options, part of a broader rotation her husband made into 2027-dated call options on several big tech names, including a batch of Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) calls with a $120 strike price. Ackman's Pershing Square owns Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) too, with 8.56 million shares worth about $2.04 billion.

Let's dig deeper into AMZN.

AMZN Has a New Catalyst

Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN) is investing heavily in AI infrastructure. Bulls point to a new catalyst for the stock: Meta's Muse AI agent. Early third-party data suggest Muse is surpassing ChatGPT's early mobile launch in downloads and daily active users in key regions.

But what's the connection with AWS?

Muse itself is not shown to run on AWS. The potential benefit is broader: agents can make repeated model calls, retrieve information and use tools, increasing demand for computing, memory, storage and networking. An industry estimate puts their network traffic at up to 450% more than a human completing the same task. Inference is forecast to account for two-thirds of AI infrastructure capacity in 2026, up from one-third in 2023 and half in 2025. The rise of agents like Meta's Muse actually widens what companies need to buy from AWS, since running these agents day to day requires much more than just AI chips, including CPUs, networking gear, and memory and storage. That broader demand plays to Amazon's strengths through its own Graviton chips.

Bear case

Amazon's (NASDAQ:AMZN) valuation premium rests almost entirely on AWS. The cloud unit makes up just 21% of total revenue but generates about 60% of operating profit, carrying a margin near 39% versus 4% to 8% for the retail business. That concentration creates risk. Any slowdown in AI demand could negatively impact the company.

Valuation

Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) non-GAAP forward P/E sits at 30.64, more than double the sector median of 14.73, and 108% above where its peers trade. On a trailing basis, non-GAAP P/E is 33.47, versus a sector median of 14.26.

news.Title: Another Roadster Delay - But Tesla's Real Story Is Finally Turning
news.Content:
There is a running joke among Tesla watchers that the second-generation Roadster exists primarily as a rhetorical device.

Elon Musk rolled a prototype out from beneath a Semi trailer in November 2017, promised production by 2020, then spent the better part of a decade moving the date. At last November's shareholder meeting he floated a demonstration on April Fool's Day, cheerfully noting the date gave him "deniability because I can say I was just kidding."

On Monday, Tesla did it again. The reveal scheduled for this Thursday, October 1st in Waco, Texas has been pushed to October 15th.

So a measure of skepticism is thoroughly earned. Yet both the reason for this delay and the broader backdrop are more encouraging than the headline suggests — and the nearer-term catalyst is no longer the Roadster at all.

The Excuse Is Also a Disclosure

Tesla's explanation was specific: "We've been tracking the weather closely with local meteorologists, but given the severe conditions predicted and because this event can only be held outdoors, we've made the difficult decision to reschedule."

That phrase — "can only be held outdoors" — is the most revealing thing Tesla has said about this car in years. Vehicle unveilings happen indoors all the time. An event that physically cannot be held under a roof implies a demonstration requiring open air and considerable clearance, which lines up precisely with the four bright thruster plumes in Tesla's teaser image and with the SpaceX-derived cold-gas thruster package Musk has described for years.

Reports have suggested the car may briefly leave the ground under remote operation, with spectators held hundreds of yards back because the thrusters are loud enough to risk hearing damage. The FAA had restricted aircraft and drone flights over the area through October 2nd.

In other words, Tesla just indirectly confirmed that the demonstration is what the rumor mill said it was. That is not nothing after nine years of vagueness.

There is a second, harder signal. Tesla has reopened Roadster reservations, and the terms are serious: a $50,000 deposit — $5,000 by credit card followed by a $45,000 wire transfer — with $250,000 required for the Founders Series. Companies do not collect wire transfers of that size for vehicles they have no intention of building.

The Nearer Catalyst Is Friday

With the reveal pushed to October 15th, the more immediate event is Tesla's third-quarter delivery report, due this Friday — and the setup there is genuinely interesting.

Wall Street consensus sits near 454,000 vehicles, but the dispersion is extraordinary: estimates run from roughly 422,000 at the low end to 482,000 at the high, a 60,000-unit spread. Goldman Sachs is at 435,000 after cutting from 490,000. Prediction markets on Kalshi have been running around 480,000.

Story Continues

The Street's recent track record here is poor. Tesla's TSLA company-compiled consensus for the second quarter was 406,024 deliveries. The actual figure came in at 480,126 — a beat of 74,000 units, with Kalshi traders landing almost exactly right. When professional forecasters have been that wrong that recently, and estimates have been cut aggressively into the print, the bar is low. Analysts suggest a figure above 485,000 would constitute a real upside surprise.

The Shift That Actually Matters

Here is the development that best supports a constructive view, and it has nothing to do with the Roadster.

Earlier this month, Goldman Sachs cut its third-quarter delivery forecast by 55,000 units, citing softness in China, the United States and Europe. Not long ago, a reduction of that size from a bank of that influence would have sent the shares sharply lower.

It barely moved.

That non-reaction tells you the market has stopped valuing Tesla primarily on how many cars it sells. Investors have repriced the company around autonomy, robotics and energy. Whether that framework is correct is debatable — the car business still funds everything else. But it means the delivery weakness that has weighed on sentiment all year is losing its power over the stock, and that removes the single largest overhang on the shares.

What's Actually Working

Beneath the margin noise, the second quarter delivered real operational progress. Robotaxi service now operates in seven U.S. markets, with Nevada approving fleet expansion to as many as 5,000 vehicles. Cybercab production has begun at Gigafactory Texas. Full Self-Driving subscriptions reached 1.48 million, up 56% year over year, with attach rates near 55% of new North American deliveries. Musk has said robotaxi miles are growing more than 10% per week.

Beyond that: an Optimus production line at Fremont, Semi commissioning in Nevada, Megapack 3 arriving for 2026, a significant Semi order recently booked, and a potential European approval of unsupervised FSD that would represent a major regulatory unlock.

Bottom Line

Tesla spent most of 2026 being judged on the one metric it can no longer easily grow — quarterly car deliveries — while the businesses meant to justify its valuation remained promises. That equation is finally shifting. Robotaxi is live in seven cities, Cybercab is in production, FSD adoption is compounding, and the market has demonstrably stopped punishing delivery cuts.

The Roadster slipping two weeks is an annoyance, not a thesis-breaker. If anything, a company that reschedules rather than stages a compromised indoor version of an event it has promised for nine years is behaving like one that intends to deliver something worth watching.

news.Title: How Tesla Semi could add billions to the EV maker's financials
news.Content:
While the big reveal of the long-awaited Tesla ( TSLA ) Roadster being pushed out until Oct. 15 due to weather probably has the hardcore Tesla bulls sad, they should get over it quickly.

With solid new numbers behind the ramp-up, Tesla's growth looks impressive.

"Tesla can generate ~$12-18k/month from its autonomous trucking software ($0.85-$1/mile subscription fee x 18k miles driven per month). This compares to ~$100/month for full self-driving on consumer vehicles today. If Tesla reaches 82k Semis on road by 2040 (13.5% share of the autonomous addressable market), that would represent $17 billion of software revenue and ~$7.5 billion of incremental EBIT (10% upside to our base case)," Morgan Stanley analyst Andrew Percoco calculated in a new note.

Percoco added, "Note that this does not include the upfront sale of the vehicle or incremental revenues for Tesla charging. Recall, Tesla originally outlined a manufacturing target of 50,000 Semi trucks per year, therefore assuming 80k will be deployed in total over the next ~15 years is a conservative starting point, in our view."

Tesla's long-delayed Semi finally hit a major milestone over the past five days: The company opened its dedicated factory in Sparks, Nev., and began customer deliveries.

Tesla said the plant is designed to eventually produce 50,000 Semis annually. The truck is offered with claimed ranges of 325 miles and 500 miles for the long-range version.

Early customers include PepsiCo ( PEP ), DHL, and US Foods ( USFD ), while a newly announced 2,500-truck order from a shipper coalition further increases potential demand.

"We see Semi as an underappreciated avenue for Tesla to expand its autonomy capabilities, with impressive unit economics that support a strong demand outlook," Percoco said.
